description: The detector systematically looks for what is missing: archive regions with no coverage, questions no tool can answer, capability combinations nobody provides. description: Coverage is modeled as a grid over subjects, capabilities, languages, and time: each cell records what exists and how well. A gap is a cell that expectation says should be filled but is not — with the expectation's reasoning attached, so gaps are argued, not asserted.

title: Expectation-based gap finding algorithm
description: Gaps are found by comparing coverage against expectations derived from population, economic weight, scientific activity, and analogies to covered areas. If a language with two million speakers has zero agricultural records while similar languages have hundreds, that asymmetry is a detected gap with quantified evidence.

title: Reasoning: is this gap real and does it matter

title: Security: gaps as sensitive information
description: Some gaps are sensitive — revealing exactly what intelligence is missing helps adversaries. Gap dossiers carry sensitivity markings, sensitive gaps are summarized rather than detailed, and access is controlled. The detector never publishes a gap whose disclosure harms the people it aims to help.
